text.en:
Ananya looked at the blackboard, the round wall clock and a folded samosa snack.
"Everything around us hides a flat shape!" she smiled.

Flat shapes appear in objects we see every day at home and school.
A wheel, coin or bangle shows a circle with a curved edge and no corners. A chessboard square or handkerchief shows a square with 4 equal sides and 4 corners.
A door, notebook or pencil box shows a rectangle with opposite sides equal. A slice of sandwich, flag pennant or traffic yield sign shows a triangle with 3 sides and 3 corners.
Look closely around your room—almost every everyday object has a shape hidden on its flat face.
A bicycle wheel, a one-rupee coin, a chapati and a round wall clock all show a circle.
Trace a coin with your pencil: a circle has one smooth curved edge and zero straight corners.
Now look at a sheet of paper, a classroom blackboard or your bedroom door—each has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners.
In a rectangle, the two longer opposite sides match in length, and the two shorter opposite sides match too.

board.text: Opposite sides of rectangle are equal

text.en: Think of a chessboard, a biscuit or a square handkerchief: here all 4 straight sides are equal!
Look at a half-cut sandwich, a hanging cloth pennant or a road warning board: count 3 straight sides and 3 corners—that is a triangle!
Even solid boxes carry flat faces! Trace the bottom of a matchbox to get a rectangle, or trace a dice face to get a square.

board.text: Tracing solid faces reveals flat shapes

text.en: Spot the difference cleanly: a square has 4 equal sides, while a rectangle has opposite sides equal.
Walk around school and count how many circles, triangles, squares and rectangles you can spot on windows, tiles and books!

problem.en: You trace the bottom of a matchbox and then trace a bangle. What two shapes do you draw?

text.en: Look at the flat bottom face of the matchbox.

why.en: Two long edges match and two short edges match, with 4 straight corners—that makes a rectangle.
It goes smoothly all the way round with no sharp corner—that makes a circle.
The matchbox bottom draws a rectangle and the bangle draws a circle.

prompt.en: A friend says a long classroom whiteboard is a square because it has 4 corners. How will you gently correct them?

requiredIdeas.en: A whiteboard has 4 corners, yet its long and short sides are different.
A square needs all 4 sides equal; a whiteboard is a rectangle.

commonMisconceptions.en: Any 4-corner shape is automatically a square.

points.en: Triangle: 3 sides and 3 corners (sandwich slice, road sign).
Square: 4 equal sides and 4 corners (dice face).
Rectangle: 4 sides with opposite sides equal (book, door).
